  "text": "The council sent a man to count the doors in our house.

“Fire regulations,” he said, showing me a badge without a photograph.

I followed him with a notebook. Front door, back door, kitchen, bathroom. He counted the cupboard beneath the stairs twice.

“That’s only one door,” I said.

“From this side.”

Upstairs, he stopped outside my daughter’s bedroom.

“Does this one still open?”

“Of course.”

He made a mark on his clipboard.

“Try not to let her close it tonight.”

After he left, I checked his figures. Eleven doors. I counted ten.

At dinner, Lucy asked why the man had measured her.

“He didn’t measure you.”

“He did while you were getting his tea. He said I’d fit.”

I took her to sleep in my room. At midnight, someone knocked inside the wardrobe.

Lucy sat up.

“That’s not ours,” she whispered.

The knocking moved to the bedroom door.

My husband’s voice asked to come in.

He was asleep beside me. I could feel his breath against my wrist.

Then the voice became mine.

“Lucy, sweetheart. You’ll make us late.”

Something slid beneath the door: a council inspection form.

Ten boxes had been ticked.

The eleventh was labelled OCCUPIED.

Below it, in my daughter’s careful handwriting, someone had written: Opens outwards.

The hinges began to lift from the frame.

I grabbed Lucy and shook my husband awake.

He looked at the door, then at the wardrobe.

“Which one did he count twice?” he asked.

Before I could answer, he climbed into the wardrobe and pulled it shut.

The knocking stopped.

In the morning, there were nine doors."
